summary: Howard Hughes Holdings reports large, uneven quarters, holds much more cash than a year ago and trades near the bottom of its short valuation history. A director who is executive chairman of Vantage bought $1.6 million of shares in September 2026. Lumpy revenue overstates the expectations gap; the contracted backlog is the steadier gauge.

facts.text: Trailing-twelve-month revenue was $2.373 billion, 34.0% above a year earlier [m:revenue_ttm] [m:revenue_ttm_yoy].
Revenue was $235.9 million in the March 2026 quarter and $1.122 billion in the June 2026 quarter [m:revenue:2026-03-31] [m:revenue:2026-06-30].
RPO was $3.8 billion at 2026-06-30, down from $4.6 billion at 2026-03-31 and 15.2% above a year earlier [m:rpo:2026-06-30] [m:rpo:2026-03-31] [m:rpo_yoy].
The trailing operating margin was 21.3% and ROIC was 5.4% [m:op_margin_ttm] [m:roic].
Cash rose to $2.648 billion at 2026-06-30 from $1.441 billion at 2025-06-30 [m:cash:2026-06-30] [m:cash:2025-06-30].
Shares outstanding rose to 59.40 million at 2025-06-30 from 50.39 million at 2025-03-31 [m:shares_outstanding:2025-06-30] [m:shares_outstanding:2025-03-31].

Director Marc Grandisson, executive chairman of Vantage, bought 25,000 shares for $1.60 million on 2026-09-23, and chief operating officer Andrew D. Davis bought 1,000 shares for $64,490 the same day [m:insider:7b289ecd-2bfb-41d6-a0d4-0186cc4ac2d5] [m:insider:712942e7-2f4e-4ac8-a5f2-d787106e4893].
Cash conversion was 2.69, up from 2.36 a year earlier, and S4 fired at strength 1.0 [s:S4].

why_mispriced.text: C1 puts EV/EBIT of 13.25 and EV/sales of 2.83 around the 10th percentile of the company's own 152-week history [c:C1].
The trailing one-year return was -16.2%, at the 25th percentile of the 409-company comparison set [c:C3].
The reverse DCF (C2) reads the enterprise value as implying 1.5% annual growth [c:C2].

inferences: Inference: revenue arrives in large, uneven quarters, so year-over-year growth rates swing and say little on their own; RPO is the steadier gauge of contracted sales.
Inference: cash, equity and the share count jumped together in the June 2025 quarter, which is consistent with a large share issuance.
Inference: a sizeable personal purchase by a board member who runs another business is a confidence signal, but one buyer is thin evidence.
assumptions: Assumption: the contracted backlog converts to revenue at margins similar to recent years.
Assumption: the cash raised is invested at returns above the current ROIC.
Assumption: there is no further large share issuance.

risks.text: Lumpy revenue pushes the C2 evidence-growth input to its 40% cap, so the expectations gap is likely overstated [c:C2] [m:revenue_q_yoy].
Total debt appears only at year ends in the pack, so net debt pairs a December 2025 debt figure with June 2026 cash [m:net_debt] [m:total_debt:2025-12-31].
The share count rose 6.9% over the year [m:shares_yoy].

kill_criteria.why: A contracted backlog smaller than a year earlier would undercut the growth case.
Dilution above 10% a year would mean growth is being bought with new shares.
A margin under 10% would mean the sales in the backlog are less profitable than assumed.
